 Order
% 12.04.2023 [Physical Hearing/ Hybrid Hearing] CM APPL. 17410/2023 (Application under Section 151 CPC seeking exemption from filing the certified copies of annexures/impugned order)
1. This is an application under Section 151 CPC seeking exemption from filing the certified copies of annexures/impugned order.
2. Allowed, subject to just exceptions.
3. Application is disposed of.

The present writ petition has been filed with prayer for directions to respondent no. 1 to demarcate the land owned by the petitioner and thereby hand over the peaceful and undisputed physical possession of the identified land comprised in Khasra no. 57 (1-08) admeasuring 1 bigha and 8 biswa situated in the revenue state of Village Behlolpur, Kader Tehsil, Mehruli, New Delhi.
5. It is submitted that father of the petitioner had purchased the land in question by virtue of registered sale deed dated 17.05.1984.
Subsequently, notifications dated 23.06.1989 and 22.06.1990 were issued by the Government for acquisition of the land of the petitioner.
An award in this regard was also passed being Award no. 15/92-93 in the year 1992-1993.

sentences.text: It is submitted that however, no compensation was given to the petitioner.

Subsequently, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (2013 Act) came into being and the earlier Land Acquisition Act of 1984 was repealed.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (2013 Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. The petitioner moved the present Court by filing writ petition being W.P. (C) No. 8540/2016 seeking quashing and setting aside of award in question.

By order dated 22.02.2018, this Court in W.P. (C) No. 8540/2016 held that the acquisition proceedings pertaining to the land of the petitioner is deemed to have lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

8. It is the case on behalf of the petitioner that despite the aforesaid order and numerous efforts by the petitioner, the respondents have failed to demarcate the land of the petitioner and have not handed over the formal possession of the said plot to the petitioner.
Hence, the present writ petition has been filed.
9. Issue notice.
10. Notice is accepted by learned counsels appearing for respondent nos. 1, 2 and 4 as well as respondent no. 3.

11. Learned counsel appearing for respondent nos. 1, 2 and 4 submits that Sub Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of the area in question would also be a necessary party, since the petitioner is seeking demarcation.
12. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he has no objection for impleading SDM as party.
13. At oral request of learned counsel for the petitioner, Sub Divisional Magistrate, District South East is impleaded as a party in the present case.

15.
